assertions.name: mirror_split_is_coulomb_kernel_strong_csb_overshoots_3x
assertions.source: AME split 0.764 ≈ pp Coulomb 0.758 (r≈1.9 fm) ⇒ strong CSB ≈+0.006; #2089 strong split 1.747 = 2.3× total ⇒ kernel over-breaks charge symmetry. Fix: charge-symmetric strong bond + separate Coulomb.

description: The A=3 mirror binding split B(³H)−B(³He)=0.764 MeV is reproduced by the pp Coulomb displacement energy (e²/4πε₀r at r≈1.9 fm = 0.758 MeV), so strong CSB is ~0 (model-independent strong residual = the ~0.07 MeV Nolen–Schiffer anomaly). The #2089 log-trace kernel assigns a STRONG mirror split E₀(ε_nn−ε_pp)=2.27 MeV — 3× the total split, ~32× the Nolen–Schiffer residual (~400× the point-charge residual) — over-breaking charge symmetry. Fix direction: charge-symmetric strong bond (f_pp≈f_nn) + separate Coulomb; this also collapses the 1.78× nucleon ε-spread, restoring equal-weight coordination counting (#3557). Scope-(a) diagnosis, no re-derivation, no wiring.
